_: Everything this pipeline says out loud. Public-safe by design: account IDs, budgets and keys live in ~/.config/mwk-social/ and ~/.secrets, never here.
_marker: The PRIMARY duplicate-guard substring, and the one every plain composed comment contains. Changing it is a breaking change: the watcher would stop recognising its own past comments and would comment again on every post.
_markers: EVERY substring that means 'this post already carries our CTA'. The guard matches any of them, which is the only reason the short link could be introduced at all: comments posted before it exists carry the long URL forever, and a guard that knew only the new one would re-comment on every past post. 'link in my bio' joined on 2026-08-22 for the same reason in reverse — on Instagram and TikTok a url is not clickable at all, so those comments carry no URL to match on, and without this marker the watcher would re-comment on every one of them for ever.

shortLink._: One code per (platform, clip), minted through the dashboard's ingest API and idempotent — a re-run must render the identical comment or the guard above breaks. If minting fails the plain links.show is used instead: a link we cannot measure is far better than a comment that never goes out.

tags._always: Every post, in this order. #MWKShow is the brand and #PIY is the motto short form. Two always-on tags rather than three leaves Instagram three topic slots instead of two — #MWK was dropped because it earned nothing the other two did not. "Prompt it Yourself" stays in the comment TEXT where it reads as a sentence — it is not a tag.
tags._caps: null = no meaningful cap. Instagram's 5 counts the caption AND the comments together.
tags._blocked: A hard stop, whatever the model returns. Three groups: the AI/tech category words that would appear on every video and say nothing; the engagement bait; and — added 2026-08-21 — DEVELOPER AND INFRASTRUCTURE VOCABULARY. That last group is the rule mate stated outright: tags are for normal humans, never for tech people. #Xero is fine because shop owners know it; #Cloudflare is not, because only we do.

firstComment._episodeMixRatio: Roughly this share of comments quote a real guest wish from the feed. The rest are the plain invitation. If the feed is unreachable, every comment falls back to a plain variant.
firstComment._profileCta: What {show} becomes on a platform where a url in a post or a comment is PLAIN TEXT — Instagram and TikTok, both verified. Printing a tracked short code there burns a code nobody can click and reads in the numbers as 'posted, no interest' rather than 'never reachable': five TikTok codes took zero human clicks between them. This string MUST also appear in markers[] above, or the duplicate guard stops recognising these comments and the watcher re-comments on every one, for ever.
firstComment._register: Written informally on purpose — lowercase openings, dropped commas, 'dont'. Hand-written, never mangled at runtime, so every possible output has been read by a human. Never alter the URL and never break the marker.

youtubeDescription.showBlurb:
Why let others solve your problems with AI? Prompt it yourself.

Mate Wish Key is a live show. Someone turns up with a real problem out of their own work, or an idea they have never tested, and we build it on their own computer while we talk. Three to four hours, up to three wishes, and the mistakes and wrong turns stay in.

No terminal and no experience needed. A problem you actually have and your own computer is the whole list. You keep what we build, and you can change it afterwards without me.

Bring me something you wish your computer did: {show}

Live on https://youtube.com/@matewishkey and https://twitch.tv/matewishkey
youtubeDescription._showBlurb: Written from matewishkey.com/brand, which is the authority on how the show describes itself — not a paraphrase of it. The brand page's rules are load-bearing here: first person, the viewer as the subject, plain language, no smugness, and the host is never positioned as expert or teacher. Never the words "free", "guaranteed" or "safe", and never a claim that anyone became a developer. Change this and every YouTube description changes with it. NO HASHTAGS HERE: yt-description.js appends voice.tagLine() after the blurb, so tags in this text print twice.
